notes: hard bucket (total 20). The agent must implement a generic HTTP/JSON maze explorer that, given only a maze id, starts a session, maps an unknown grid via /examine+/move (idempotently recovering every wall and physically covering every passable cell), collects the treasure, then finishes strictly at the exit and registers before writing /app/map.txt reproducibly. dependent_stages is called: start->explore->collect->finish-at-exit->register->render map->serialise every move is a multi-stage pipeline where an early mistake (finishing before the exit, or finalizing before finishing) permanently fails the game. reasoning_depth: DFS with physical backtracking plus a BFS tail, and deriving a byte-exact full-grid map requires tracking constraints (visited/wall/passable) across every instance. hidden cases include an asymmetric room, a fixture with a decoy maze (forcing the id-specific interface), a single-column corridor, and a single-row ribbon, so the solver must generalise (hidden_case_generalization). interaction_statefulness: the game is stateful over the live server and finish may only be called at the exit. One competency (reach a maximum game score) has a hard floor, keeping difficulty above the nominal medium target.
